reviewed_by: Claude Code, fixing the linked-memory defects found in the 2026-11-19 production card audit
reason: Linked memory gave Core's goal kickoff operator authority, curated lessons that route around a required project hook, injected off-topic cards (a word and its stem both counted, and Nebula's own words and the project ID matched), and stalled 16.5 h because any background goal turn paused curation (an active turn now records its capacity lane so a queued goal turn is not mistaken for an operator's). Fixes are in linked_memory_curator/helper/rules/store. The fixed goal instruction texts moved to domain.py so the curator can recognise them. Selected: all linked-memory tests (6 new ones fail on main), product-knowledge freshness and linked-memory search (docs changed), the real worker-process kernel test (the curator runs in workers), and the goal start, resume, continuation and subagent-reports continuation paths whose instruction texts moved.
exclusions: No frontend, native or Playwright tests: nothing under ui/ changes and linked memory has no operator interface. chat.py, chat_goals.py and chat_subagents.py change only where the fixed instruction texts come from (byte-identical strings), so their suites beyond the selected start, resume, continuation and subagent-report nodes are excluded. The migration head and settings-assistant catalog are unchanged. A disposable LAN Core on 192.168.1.155 with the local Qwen3.5-2B and a slow stub model validated curation alongside a busy goal, the operator-turn pause, authority, entry matching and the saved-card re-check.
